"Create a complete, fully playable 3D political satire fighting game inspired by Sansad Showdown: The Great Kursi Fight. The game must have original implementation, professional-quality graphics and complete gameplay.

GAME TYPE:
Third-person 3D arena fighting game with single-player, local multiplayer and online multiplayer modes.

GRAPHICS:
Target AAA-quality visuals comparable to modern console fighting games. Realistic PBR materials, detailed character models, realistic skin, cloth and hair, high-quality textures, realistic shadows, global illumination, reflections, ambient occlusion, cinematic lighting, particle effects, motion blur and high-quality environmental details.

GAME SIZE:
Target final Android game size 500–600 MB. Use optimized 3D models, high-quality textures, audio, animations and compressed assets. Do not create empty filler files just to reach the size.

ENVIRONMENTS:
Build a detailed Indian Parliament-inspired fictional fighting arena, with parliamentary seating, speaker podium, wooden furniture, architectural details, decorative lights, large audience seating and animated spectators. Include multiple original arenas.

CHARACTERS:
Add EXACTLY these 9 requested characters:
1. Narendra Modi
2. Yogi Adityanath
3. Nitin Gadkari
4. Ravi Kishan
5. Lalu Prasad Yadav
6. Rahul Gandhi
7. Mamata Banerjee
8. Mahatma Gandhi
9. Donald Trump

Remove all previously suggested fictional characters. Do not add extra playable characters. Create recognizable, respectful, clearly fictionalized satirical 3D game representations of all nine people. Give each a distinct costume, appearance, fighting style, idle animation, special moves and victory animation. Mahatma Gandhi should have a playful historical-inspired non-violent representation.

GAMEPLAY:
Include punch, kick, block, dodge, grab, combos, special attacks, stamina, health bars, knockback and responsive hit reactions. Smooth transitions and responsive controls.

MODES:
1. Story Mode
2. Quick Fight
3. Tournament Mode
4. 1v1 Mode
5. Multiplayer Mode
6. Training Mode

MOBILE CONTROLS:
Virtual joystick on left, punch, kick, block, dodge and special attack buttons on right. Add camera control and controller support.

ANIMATIONS:
High-quality fighting animations, idle animations, walking, running, jumping, attacking, blocking, falling, getting up and victory poses.

AUDIO:
Original background music, arena ambience, audience reactions, fictional character voice lines, hit sounds and menu sounds.

AI:
Create intelligent CPU opponents with multiple difficulty levels, tactical attacks, blocking, dodging and combos.

ANDROID OPTIMIZATION:
Target Android 15, 64-bit ARM devices. Include adjustable graphics settings, low/medium/high/ultra presets, stable frame rate, optimized memory usage, loading screens and pause menu.

UI:
Create a polished professional fighting game interface with character selection, arena selection, health bars, settings, game modes, loading screen and main menu.

DELIVERABLE:
Build the complete working game, not a prototype or mockup. Include all source files, assets, project configuration, Android build configuration and a properly signed release APK. Test gameplay, controls, collisions, menus, loading and Android compatibility. Fix errors before delivery.

IMPORTANT:
Do not leave placeholder characters, missing textures, unfinished buttons or fake gameplay. Every advertised feature must actually work. If a feature cannot be implemented, clearly report it rather than pretending it works.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D political-satire fighting game inspired by Sansad Showdown.
- User asked for the game now, with no clarification questions, and requested limitations be reported honestly.

## Requirements
- Exactly nine named fighters; original fictionalized satire and a playful, non-violent Gandhi representation.
- 3D arenas, fighting gameplay, CPU opponents, listed game modes, mobile/controller controls, audio, polished UI, and Android optimization.
- Requested a 500–600 MB Android game and properly signed release APK, with working source, assets, configuration, and compatibility tests.
- No placeholder or falsely advertised features; test the gameplay and report anything unimplemented.

## Decisions
- Implemented an original browser game using Three.js and procedural geometry/materials instead of external character assets.
- Online multiplayer is explicitly marked “ONLINE · SOON”; “1V1 LOCAL” and “MULTIPLAYER” are local two-player modes.
- Existing procedural experience does not claim to be AAA quality or a native Android release.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a Vite/Three.js game with a main menu, nine-character selection roster, three procedural arenas, match selection, CPU/local matches, controls, combat, HUD, pause/result screens, and synthesized sound/voice barks.
- `npm install` succeeded; `npm run build` succeeded, with a large-chunk warning.
- Changes are uncommitted.

### Active
- Browser/gameplay verification; a dev server was started with `npm run dev -- --port 3002`.
- Inspect the UI and fix runtime or interaction issues before reporting.

### Blocked
- Native Android project, signed release APK, Android 15/ARM validation, 500–600 MB asset delivery, true online multiplayer, high-fidelity sourced assets/animations, and comprehensive mobile/controller testing are not implemented.
- No screenshot or browser test has yet been performed.

## Next Move
1. Open the running game at `http://localhost:3002`, check browser console/runtime behavior, and save/read a current small JPEG screenshot.
2. Test roster selection, arena/mode selection, CPU combat, keyboard and touch controls, pause/rematch, and local 1v1; fix issues found.
3. Rebuild and report the browser build’s implemented features and the unimplemented Android/online/AAA requirements clearly.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, fighter/arena/mode selection, HUD, mobile controls, overlays.
- `src/main.js`: Procedural Three.js arenas/fighters, gameplay, CPU logic, controls, audio, and UI behavior.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `package-lock.json`: Installed dependency lockfile.

## Important Context
- Build command was `npm install && npm run build`; Vite produced `dist/` and warned that the minified JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- User expressly asked not to claim unimplemented features work; in particular, no signed APK or native Android build exists.

- Build a complete, playable 3D political-satire fighting game inspired by Sansad Showdown.

- Built an original browser game with Three.js and procedural geometry/materials instead of external character assets.

- The current procedural browser game does not claim AAA quality or native Android support.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D political-satire fighting game inspired by Sansad Showdown, and test it before reporting.
- Be candid about missing features, especially native Android delivery and online multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Exactly nine named fighters; original fictionalized satire and a playful, non-violent Gandhi representation.
- 3D arenas, combat, CPU opponents, listed game modes, mobile/controller controls, audio, polished UI, and Android optimization.
- Requested a 500–600 MB Android game and properly signed release APK with working source, assets, configuration, and compatibility tests.
- No placeholder or falsely advertised features.

## Decisions
- Built an original browser game with Three.js and procedural geometry/materials instead of external character assets.
- Online multiplayer is explicitly marked “ONLINE · SOON”; “1V1 LOCAL” and “MULTIPLAYER” are local two-player modes.
- The procedural browser game does not claim AAA quality or native Android support.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, nine-fighter roster, three arenas, match selection, CPU/local matches, combat, HUD, pause/result screens, and synthesized audio/voice barks.
- Fixed local movement conflict in `inputMove()`: player 1 uses WASD/mobile controls; player 2 uses arrow keys.
- Added `public/favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html`; preview serves it with HTTP 200.
- `npm run build` succeeds; Chromium headless loads the game and renders the initialized Three.js canvas/menus. Preview and favicon requests return HTTP 200.

### Active
- Continue browser testing of local 1v1 controls, CPU gameplay, pause/resume, rematch/results, and mobile layout. Chromium remote debugging is running, but interactive CDP checks are not yet completed.
- Investigate the existing large-chunk build warning and Three.js deprecated shadow-map warning if practical.

### Blocked
- Native Android project, signed release APK, Android 15/ARM validation, and 500–600 MB asset delivery are not implemented.
- True online multiplayer, high-fidelity sourced assets/animations, and comprehensive mobile/controller testing are not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Use the running Chromium remote-debugging session to test local player controls, pause/resume, and match flow; check for browser errors.
2. Check mobile layout and touch controls; fix any issues found.
3. Re-run `npm run build` and report browser features versus unimplemented Android/online requirements clearly.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, procedural fighters/arenas, combat, CPU, and input handling.
- `index.html`: UI structure, fighter/mode selection, HUD, mobile controls, and overlays.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive styling and mobile layout.
- `public/favicon.svg`: Added game favicon.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

## Important Context
- Build output is about 528 kB minified JavaScript and reports a chunk-size warning.
- Earlier browser testing found a missing-favicon 404 and a deprecated Three.js shadow-map warning; the favicon 404 is now addressed.
- Changes are uncommitted; the repository initially showed project files as untracked. Screenshots exist at `screenshots/menu.png` and `screenshots/fight.png`.

## Objective
- Build and test a playable 3D political-satire fighting game inspired by Sansad Showdown.
- Clearly disclose that native Android delivery and online multiplayer are not included.

## Requirements
- Exactly nine named fighters, original fictionalized satire, and a playful, non-violent Gandhi representation.
- 3D arenas, combat, CPU opponents, listed game modes, mobile/controller controls, audio, polished UI, and Android optimization.
- Requested a 500–600 MB Android game and signed release APK with source, assets, configuration, and compatibility tests.
- Do not claim features that are not implemented.

## Decisions
- Built an original browser game with Three.js and procedural geometry/materials instead of external character assets.
- Online multiplayer is explicitly marked “ONLINE · SOON”; “1V1 LOCAL” and “MULTIPLAYER” are local two-player modes.
- The browser game does not claim AAA quality or native Android support.
- Reduced arena lighting/shadows and audience geometry to improve performance; increased the simulation delta cap from 0.04 to 0.1 seconds.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, nine-fighter roster, three arenas, match selection, CPU/local matches, combat, HUD, pause/result screens, and synthesized audio/voice barks.
- Fixed local movement conflict in `inputMove()`: Player 1 uses WASD/mobile controls; Player 2 uses arrow keys.
- Added `public/favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html`.
- Prior `npm run build` succeeded; Chromium checks verified menu/roster navigation, local fight entry, pause/resume/quit, no console errors, and no horizontal overflow at 390×844.
- Verified close-range local combat damages both fighters; Player 1 and Player 2 health dropped to 91% and 89.7%.

### Active
- Remove the temporary `window.__sansadDebug` function added to `src/main.js` for combat testing.
- Rebuild and verify match completion/results and rematch after cleanup.

### Blocked
- Native Android project, signed release APK, Android 15/ARM validation, and requested 500–600 MB delivery are not implemented.
- True online multiplayer, high-fidelity sourced assets/animations, and comprehensive mobile/controller testing are not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Remove temporary `window.__sansadDebug` exposure from `src/main.js`.
2. Run `npm run build`; check warnings and rerun browser checks.
3. Verify match results and rematch if feasible; report browser features separately from unimplemented Android/online requirements.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, procedural fighters/arenas, combat, CPU, and input handling.
- `index.html`: UI structure, fighter/mode selection, HUD, mobile controls, and overlays.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive styling and mobile layout.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `/tmp/opencode/combat-check.cjs`: Chromium local movement/combat probe.
- `/tmp/opencode/test-sansad.cjs`: Chromium DOM and navigation checks.
- `/tmp/opencode/verify-sansad.cjs`: Mobile viewport and screenshot check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status`.
- Latest performance-related edits and temporary debug exposure have not been included in a subsequent production build.
- Chromium testing showed slow animation-frame progress in this environment; close-range combat damage was nevertheless confirmed.
- The existing chunk-size build warning and deprecated Three.js shadow-map warning may warrant review.

## Objective
- Build and test a playable 3D political-satire fighting game inspired by Sansad Showdown.
- Clearly disclose that native Android delivery and online multiplayer are not included.

## Requirements
- Exactly nine named fighters, original fictionalized satire, and a playful, non-violent Gandhi representation.
- 3D arenas, combat, CPU opponents, listed game modes, mobile/controller controls, audio, polished UI, and Android optimization.
- Requested a 500–600 MB Android game and signed release APK with source, assets, configuration, and compatibility tests.
- Do not claim features that are not implemented.

## Decisions
- Built an original browser game with Three.js and procedural geometry/materials instead of external character assets.
- Online multiplayer is explicitly marked “ONLINE · SOON”; “1V1 LOCAL” and “MULTIPLAYER” are local two-player modes.
- The browser game does not claim AAA quality or native Android support.
- Reduced arena lighting/shadows and audience geometry to improve performance; increased the simulation delta cap from 0.04 to 0.1 seconds.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, nine-fighter roster, three arenas, match selection, CPU/local matches, combat, HUD, pause/result screens, and synthesized audio/voice barks.
- Fixed local movement conflict in `inputMove()`: Player 1 uses WASD/mobile controls; Player 2 uses arrow keys.
- Added `public/favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html`.
- Removed temporary `window.__sansadDebug` exposure from `src/main.js`.
- `npm run build` succeeded; output warns that the 527.94 kB JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- Earlier Chromium checks verified menu/roster navigation, local fight entry, pause/resume/quit, no console errors, and no horizontal overflow at 390×844.
- Earlier close-range local combat confirmed damage to both fighters.

### Active
- Re-run browser checks after cleanup; match completion/results and rematch remain unverified.
- Confirm the browser test environment is responsive after the attempted accelerated animation test timed out.

### Blocked
- Native Android project, signed release APK, Android 15/ARM validation, and requested 500–600 MB delivery are not implemented.
- True online multiplayer, high-fidelity sourced assets/animations, and comprehensive mobile/controller testing are not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Re-establish a responsive Chromium session and rerun the basic navigation, local combat, and mobile-layout checks.
2. Verify match result and rematch if feasible; confirm the debug hook is absent in the built app.
3. Report implemented browser features separately from unimplemented Android and online requirements.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, procedural fighters/arenas, combat, CPU, and input handling.
- `index.html`: UI structure, fighter/mode selection, HUD, mobile controls, and overlays.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive styling and mobile layout.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `/tmp/opencode/test-sansad.cjs`: Chromium navigation and responsive-layout checks.
- `/tmp/opencode/combat-check.cjs`: Local movement/combat probe.
- `/tmp/opencode/verify-results.cjs`: Match completion/rematch probe; currently uses an accelerated animation-frame override that timed out.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status`.
- The last normal results probe did not finish a match: timer reached 77, with player/opponent health at 88.4286% and 79.4286%; rematch was therefore not tested.
- The accelerated animation-frame override caused the results probe and subsequent browser check to time out; Chromium was killed and relaunched, but responsiveness was not confirmed.
